description.narrative: The AACJ consortium in Somalia will work from a movement building perspective and focus on increasing the knowledge of existing CSOs around climate change and the prospect of climate justice policies. Broadening the partner base and effectively linking local organizations in Somaliland is fundamental to movement building (Pathway 1). Activities related to this objective include developing online and offline platforms to share knowledge between humanitarian organizations, women, youth and minority groups. Another priority is to raise awareness of CSOs and citizens on climate justice rights, including facilitating the participation of climate activists in media discussions and policy debates about climate justice in the regional and national context (Pathway 2). With the support of Natural Justice, the consortium will look for opportunities to develop legal empowerment approaches for communities (for example a paralegal programme and community audits) to defend their rights.

participating-org.narrative: In 2004 Oxfam Novib set up a Liaison Office in Nairobi, Kenya in order to support the Strengthening Somali Civil Society Program, at the request of the EU. This request was based on Oxfam Novib's work in Somalia to date, but intended to be more widely directed atthe entire civil society sector and the specific context in which it is operating in a post-conflict country. The program started with consulting local organisations in Somalia and Somaliland to get a complete picture of the sectors and regions where they are active, the challenges they face and the relationship between civil society, local political structures and the private sector. A program was then developed to strengthen the institutional development of Oxfam Novib's partners and those of other Oxfams, as well as a range of new NGOs. In the first year local consultants were trained in Somalia. They were then seconded to civil society organisations to build their capacity in financial and organisational management. Furthermore, workshops were organised on specific themes suchas human rights and the role of civil society in the Somali context. The Liaison Office is now going to support the expansion of the program, focussing on strengthening both organisation and project management, while facilitating more training in the fields of civic education, governance, human rights and women's rights, HIV and AIDS and child protection. Over the years, the Somalia Country Office has expanded its intervention on short term humanitarian response as well as development development interventions. In 2015/2016, a decision was reached to move the Country Programme operation, which was largely in Nairobi, from Nairobi to Hargeisa. The country office has a small office in Nairobi , Kenya and large operations office in Hargeisa, Somaliland.

comment.narrative: Oxfam Somalia, through the AACJ, played a pivotal role in supporting the Ministry of Environment and Climate Change in convening three weeks of consultations for the development of NDC-3.0. This involved a series of workshops and meetings that brought together representatives from CSOs, the private sector, academia, and various line ministries. The consultations reached over 115 people from CSOs, women, youth, and government. Despite this encouraging effort from the Ministry of Environment in advancing climate action, there is still a lack of a participatory approach to ensuring the voices of marginalized groups, such as women, youth, people with disabilities, and indigenous communities, are included

comment.narrative:
Oxfam hosted events to celebrate World Environment Day on June 5, 2024, including workshops in Mogadishu and Hargeisa, attended by 24 and 51 participants respectively. Between August and November 2024. Oxfam organized a vibrant event in partnership with the Somaliland Women’s Resource Center. This gathering brought together over 50 participants, including youth, women, climate activists, government officials, and civil society leaders.
- Between November 11th and 22nd, 2024, Oxfam Somali supported four delegates representing Somali CSOs to attend COP 29 in Baku, Azerbaijan. These delegates, primarily from minority groups, youth-led organizations, women, and Oxfam's strategic local partners, actively participated in various sessions and side events. They engaged in high-level discussions on climate justice, climate finance, and loss and damage, aiming to influence global climate policies. The delegates focused on advocating for increased climate finance to support adaptation and mitigation efforts in Somalia, emphasizing the need for equitable and inclusive climate policies. They met with , Oxfam Team at COP29, key donors, international policymakers, and representatives from other nations to highlight the unique challenges faced by Somalia due to climate change. Their participation ensured that the voices of marginalized communities were heard, and they pushed for commitments to address the specific needs of vulnerable populations in Somalia. Through their efforts, the delegates aimed to secure more substantial support and resources for climate action in Somalia, ensuring that global climate policies reflect the realities and priorities of those most affected by climate change.
-Oxfam supported the Ministry of Environment and Climate Change in developing NDC-3.0 through consultations and hosted a national conference on climate resilience and the role of Somali women, attended by over 150 women from various institutions.

comment.narrative: In our aim to promote locally led action in Somalia, Oxfam Partnered with 5 CSOs based across Somali .The CSOs spearhead key events including workshops, training sessions, and community engagement activities aimed at advancing climate action and justice. For instance, Somaliland women resource center hosted an "Empowering Women for Climate Justice" workshop on July 14, 2024, with 57 female beneficiaries, and Green Hope movement in Puntland , Somalia organized a "Climate Action Consultation" on August 5,2024, bringing together 85 participants. Other notable events include Arlaadi organization’s "Climate-Smart Agriculture" campaign on July 23, 2024, which engaged 25 farmers, and Action 4 Environment in Mogadishu , Banadir region book exhibition on September 12, 2024, promoting climate education through children's literature, reaching 103 participants. These events demonstrate the collaborative efforts of various CSOs, advocacy groups, and community members in empowering different segments of the population, including women, youth, and rural communities, to address climate challenges in Somalia and Somaliland.

Puntland State University (PSU) Climate Workshop – held in Garowe, 21–24 June 2025, involving 80 university students (38 men, 42 women), connecting PSU’s Climate Resilience Center (CRC) with academia and youth networks.
Hargeisa University Media & Climate Training – Conducted in Hargeisa, 13–14 May 2025, with 40 journalism students trained (gender disaggregation not specified), linking academic institutions and climate justice narratives.
Action for Environment Community Workshop – Organized inMogadishu on 1 June 2025, involving 40 participants (18 men, 22 women), bringing together CBOs, local activists, and residents.
AEHRO Public Debate – Held in Baidoa on 19 June 2025, involving 20 participants (10 men, 10 women), connecting CSOs, civil society, and local government to discuss climate justice and economic policy.
